reconstructed_theorem_text: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product normed vector space E equipped with its Borel measurable structure and every real polynomial p, let gamma=stdGaussian(E), the actual centered standard Gaussian on E. Define f(w,x)=p.eval(inner_product(w,x)) and df(w,v,x)=p.derivative.eval(inner_product(w,x))*inner_product(v,x) for all w,v,x in E, where p.derivative is the literal polynomial derivative. Then there exist one family hf proving MemLp(f(w,.),2,gamma) for every w in E, one family hdf proving MemLp(df(w,v,.),2,gamma) for every w,v in E, and a map D assigning to each w in E an actual continuous real linear operator D(w):E->L2(gamma), such that both of the following hold. For every w,v in E, D(w)(v)=(hdf(w,v)).toLp(df(w,v,.)), the actual L2(gamma) equivalence class of that displayed scalar derivative function. For every w in E, the map F:E->L2(gamma), F(u)=(hf(u)).toLp(f(u,.)), has Frechet derivative D(w) at w in the full ambient normed space E. Equivalently, as nonzero h in E tends to zero, norm_{L2(gamma)}(F(w+h)-F(w)-D(w)(h))/norm_E(h) tends to zero; the remainder is little-o of norm_E(h). All parameter vectors and directions range over the whole E, with no unit-norm or one-dimensional-curve restriction. The Gaussian and input variable space remain fixed as w and h vary. Both L2-membership families and the continuous-linear derivative operators are produced conclusions, not supplied integrability or derivative assumptions. MemLp gives almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L2 seminorm. toLp denotes the genuine class of the specified raw function under gamma-almost-everywhere equality; its value does not depend on the membership proof. The operator-value identity is an equality of L2 classes, without requiring a chosen representative of D(w)(v) to equal the raw derivative function at every x. The family D has type E->(E->L[R]L2(gamma)): each D(w) is continuous and linear in its direction argument, but the statement does not separately assert continuity of w->D(w) in operator norm. The only supplied assumptions are the displayed space structures and p; no sign, degree, nonzero-polynomial, positive-dimensionality, bound, or prior differentiability premise is present. No explicit estimate constant or quantitative derivative modulus is specified.
objects: Finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space E with its Borel measurable structure; real polynomial p and its literal polynomial derivative; fixed standard Gaussian gamma on E; raw functions f(w,x)=p.eval(inner_product(w,x)) and df(w,v,x)=p.derivative.eval(inner_product(w,x))*inner_product(v,x); global L2-membership proof families hf,hdf; the actual L2-class map F; and a derivative assignment D whose value at each w is a continuous real linear map from E to L2(gamma).
domains: E has NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, FiniteDimensional R, MeasurableSpace, and BorelSpace structures. p:Polynomial R is arbitrary. gamma=stdGaussian(E) is the actual standard Gaussian under that measurable structure. All w,u,v,h,x range over the full E. Each raw f(w,.) and df(w,v,.) maps E to R. The quotient target is Lp R 2 gamma with its norm topology. D:E->(E->L[R]Lp R 2 gamma) uses actual continuous real linear maps with their operator norm. No positive dimension or unit-vector restriction appears; completeness of E follows from finite dimensionality over R, without a separately supplied CompleteSpace instance in the statement.
quantifiers: For every E with the displayed structures and every p, first let gamma,f,df have the fixed displayed definitions. There exist hf:forall w:E, MemLp(f(w,.),2,gamma), hdf:forall w,v:E, MemLp(df(w,v,.),2,gamma), and D:E->(E->L[R]Lp R 2 gamma). These same global witnesses satisfy a conjunction: for every w,v the operator identity holds, and for every w the full class map F formed with hf has Frechet derivative D(w) at w. The witnesses are selected before the final universal quantifiers. hf,hdf are proofs of membership of already specified functions, not choices of replacement functions or measures.
assumptions: Only the displayed real inner-product normed, finite-dimensional, and Borel measurable-space structures on E, and an arbitrary given real polynomial p. Genuine L2 membership of both raw function families, existence of actual continuous linear derivative maps, and the Frechet differentiability conclusions are not hypotheses. No scalar-curve derivative, ridge integrability, unit-weight constraint, norm bound, sign condition, positive polynomial degree, nonzero polynomial, or positive-dimensionality premise is supplied.
conclusion: There are global hf and hdf proving actual Gaussian L2 membership of f(w,.) for all w and of df(w,v,.) for all w,v. There is D assigning a continuous real linear operator to each w. For every w,v, its value on v is exactly the L2(gamma) class of x->p.derivative.eval(inner_product(w,x))*inner_product(v,x). For every w, F(u)=[x->p.eval(inner_product(u,x))] has full ambient Frechet derivative D(w) at w: norm_{L2(gamma)}(F(w+h)-F(w)-D(w)(h)) is little-o of norm_E(h) as h tends to zero.
scopes: The same actual Gaussian gamma is used for every L2 class and every norm in the derivative remainder. w is the differentiation base point, v is any direction used to identify the operator, h is an arbitrary small ambient vector increment, and x is the raw-function input governed by gamma. The derivative is full Frechet differentiability in E, rather than only along one chosen direction or within a parameter subset. Membership proofs give the actual almost-everywhere classes, so their selected representatives need agree with raw f or df only gamma-almost everywhere; proof choices do not change those classes. For each fixed w, D(w) is genuinely real linear and continuous in v. The type E->(E->L[R]L2(gamma)) imposes no separately asserted continuity of the derivative assignment in w. The statement covers arbitrary finite dimension, including zero, with the usual full-space Frechet convention. There are no parameter-measure integrals or scalar averaging operations in the statement.
constant_dependencies: The derivative formula has exactly the product p.derivative.eval(inner_product(w,x))*inner_product(v,x), with no extra scalar factor or normalization. F and D are determined mathematically by E,p and the fixed gamma; membership proofs do not alter their class values. Each operator D(w) is bounded because it is continuous linear, but no explicit operator-norm bound, uniform-in-w constant, Lipschitz rate, or numeric modulus for the little-o remainder is stated. No unspecified estimate constant is introduced.
